marker_future: Unicode CLDR, locale ta, dateFields.json, field the in-N patterns of every unit.
The in-N-units pattern carries NO preposition: the direction is the
LOCATIVE suffix -இல் on the unit itself ({0} ஆண்டில், {0} நாட்களில்).
The numeral fold cuts that suffix off the unit word and emits it as this
separate marker, so the engine reads the fused surface as the unit plus a
forward direction.  A bare இல் is never written on its own in Tamil, so
the surface is unreachable except from that split.

marker_past: Unicode CLDR, locale ta, dateFields.json, field the ago patterns of every unit.
முன் "before" closes the ago pattern, following the dative-marked unit
({0} ஆண்டிற்கு முன்).  It is shipped only in that trailing role, because
no source consulted attested it as a free-standing preposition.

marker_weekday_counted_ambiguous: திங்கள் names Monday, the moon, the month and -- obsoletely -- the week,
so a COUNT before it ("இரண்டு திங்கள்") can only be a span of months;
nobody counts Mondays that way.  This locale reads the month unit as
மாதம், CLDR's own wording, and ships no month sense for திங்கள், so the
count vetoes the weekday reading instead: answering "Monday" to "two
months" would give a caller who asked for a duration one specific day.
Declining the false weekday reading is not the same as asserting the
unshipped month one, which stays unavailable.

unit_day: Unicode CLDR, locale ta, dateFields.json, field day.
A counted noun is CASE-MARKED in Tamil, not bare: the ago pattern is
the DATIVE unit plus முன், and the in-N pattern is the LOCATIVE on
the unit with no preposition at all.  Both case forms are unit
surfaces in their own right, and both are CLDR's own wording.
The plural stem is suppletive in shape (நாள் -> நாட்கள்).  நாள் and
நாளை (tomorrow) differ by one grapheme and both stand next to a
numeral, so the day-word file carries only the unit senses.
unit_hour: Unicode CLDR, locale ta, dateFields.json, field hour.
A counted noun is CASE-MARKED in Tamil, not bare: the ago pattern is
the DATIVE unit plus முன், and the in-N pattern is the LOCATIVE on
the unit with no preposition at all.  Both case forms are unit
surfaces in their own right, and both are CLDR's own wording.
மணிநேரம் does not inflect for count in either direction -- CLDR gives
the same wording for one hour and for N.  The everyday மணி is NOT a
unit surface: its first dictionary sense is "bell", so it is read as
an hour only beside a numeral, which the numeral fold does.
